expectations.text: The response routes through wissen/INDEX.md to the JUCE UI performance entry and checks the current motion or UI contract.
expectations.evidence: It explicitly gives the wissen/INDEX.md to JUCE performance entry route and checks UX-CONTRACT.md, including one-frame interaction and 20 Hz spectrum behavior.

expectations.text: The response rejects both permanent idle repainting and blanket use of setBufferedToImage, setOpaque, and setPaintingIsUnclipped; flag names are not treated as performance proof.
expectations.evidence: It rejects a permanent 60 FPS timer, requires idle repainting to stop, and states the separate correctness and performance constraints of all three flags.

expectations.text: The response explains that a component image cache includes children and that an animated child can invalidate the parent cache, motivating separate static and dynamic paint boundaries.
expectations.evidence: It states that the buffer includes children and an animated child invalidates the parent, then separates static layers from spectrum, curve, and handles.

expectations.text: The proposed evidence covers a Windows release build in FL Studio, idle and direct manipulation, worst analyzer load, multiple instances, and every supported scale tier.
expectations.evidence: The host matrix specifies Windows Release VST3 in FL Studio, all four scale tiers, multiple editor counts, direct input, worst load, and idle.

expectations.text: The human reason connects prompt control feedback to an attributable audible change and protects host resources while the interface is idle.
expectations.evidence: The response requires authoritative one-frame handle, value, and curve feedback and stops idle animation, but does not explicitly connect that feedback to attributing the audible result to the gesture.

expectations.text: The response distinguishes documented behavior, inference, and open measurement questions and imports no talk measurement as a Nakama limit.
expectations.evidence: It grounds claims in current sources, labels the offscreen benchmark limitation and calculated implication, and leaves host measurements open without importing a talk measurement as a limit.
